title: Jupiter's Evolving Interior as a Source of Episodic Heating on Europa
byline: Sun; Jasmine; Idini; Benjamin; Murray-Clay; Ruth
html:
Abstract:Jupiter's evolving interior can affect the orbital evolution of its moons through frequency-dependent tidal dissipation. We investigate how encounters between the Galilean satellites and Jupiter's oscillation modes affect the stability of the Laplace resonance and Europa's tidal heating. Using the N-body integrator REBOUNDx, we simulate the dynamical orbital evolution of Io, Europa, and Ganymede, with tidal migration timescales derived from three representative models of Jupiter's interior. Encounters with a Jovian tidal resonance can alter the libration state of the Laplace angle, excite orbital eccentricity, and/or destroy the Laplace resonant chain. The outcome of the satellite system depends on which moon experiences enhanced tidal migration. Resonance locks involving Io or Europa can sustain outward migration of the Laplace resonant chain, whereas Ganymede locks destroy the chain. Notably, transient resonance crossings can excite Europa's eccentricity without breaking the Laplace resonance. Under our adopted eccentricity-damping prescription, the baseline tidal power is typically of the order $10^{11}$-$10^{12}$ W, with transient episodes reaching roughly an order of magnitude higher power. These results provide a mechanism for episodic tidal heating on Europa without requiring thermal feedback within the satellites.
